title: Sell Mineral Rights in McDonald, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in McDonald, PA | Washington County
metaDescription: McDonald, PA straddles Washington and Allegheny counties in the Marcellus core. We buy mineral rights directly and explain your royalty statement in plain terms.
heroLead: McDonald sits right on the Washington-Allegheny county line, in an old oil-boom town that's now sitting on top of one of the most productive parts of the Marcellus play.
intro: McDonald actually has oil in its history twice over. The original McDonald oil field was one of the most productive shallow fields in the country back in the 1890s, and now the deeper Marcellus shale under the same ground has brought a second wave of leasing and drilling through Cecil and Robinson townships. If you're holding mineral rights here, your family's story with this ground may run back further than you think.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around McDonald directly, and because this area has that layered oil-then-gas history, we spend real time confirming exactly which rights your deed actually covers before we make an offer.

sections.heading: A Town With Two Booms
paragraphs: The shallow oil sands that made McDonald famous in the 1890s are a different formation entirely from the Marcellus and Utica shale that operators target today, thousands of feet deeper. Some McDonald-area deeds still carry old oil and gas reservations from that first boom, which can complicate figuring out who owns what in the modern Marcellus unit.

Washington County remains one of the most heavily drilled counties in the Marcellus wet-gas window, and McDonald's position near the Allegheny County line hasn't kept operators away. Multi-well pads have gone in throughout Cecil and Robinson townships over the past fifteen years.

sections.heading: What We Check Before Making an Offer
paragraphs: We pull records from the Washington County Recorder of Deeds and, where relevant, Allegheny County, since some McDonald-area tracts straddle the line or have title history recorded on either side. That cross-county piece is one reason McDonald title work takes a little more care than a single-county property.
Once title is clear, we review your division order and any royalty statements to understand your actual decimal interest and how the well or wells are currently performing.

sections.heading: Deductions on an Old Lease
paragraphs: Older leases in this area, some originally negotiated before the current wave of Marcellus development, don't always carry the royalty protections that newer leases include. If gathering and compression costs are coming off the top of your check, Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act may still guarantee you a one-eighth floor even under an older lease, and we'll help you understand where your specific lease stands.

faqs.question: Does the old McDonald oil field affect my Marcellus rights?
faqs.answer: It can complicate title research since some deeds carry reservations from the shallow oil era, but it doesn't automatically affect your deeper Marcellus rights. We check each deed specifically rather than assuming.

faqs.question: My property is near the Allegheny County line. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can, since title records for a straddling tract may be split across two county recorders. We handle that research as part of our review at no cost to you.

faqs.question: How do you determine a fair offer?
faqs.answer: We weigh your confirmed decimal interest, recent production and royalty history, the operator's activity in your specific unit, and current market conditions for Washington County interests.
